properties.name: Third independent measurement that reflow2's FUNCTIONAL decomposition disagrees with its coupling: 80% of component dependencies cross the new subsystem groups. Expected, not a defect — a layered carving maximises cross-group edges by construction
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-25, immediately after the coherence-loop and agent-surface splits, as a deliberate check on whether a grouping arrived at BY JUDGEMENT survives contact with the dependency data.

═══ THE NUMBERS ═══

    Component -> Component DEPENDS_ON edges, whole design      72
    both ends inside the two newly split systems               15
       WITHIN a group   3   (20%)   <- cohesion
       ACROSS groups   12   (80%)   <- coupling
    one or both ends elsewhere in the design                   57

    top cross-group couplings
       4  Telling  -> Finding
       2  Finding  -> Change and structure
       2  Telling  -> Change and structure
       2  Telling  -> Evidence

⚠️ BY A MODULARITY STANDARD THIS IS POOR COHESION, AND REPORTING IT IS THE POINT. The grouping was proposed by an agent, accepted by the user, and then measured against data that could have embarrassed it. It did. That is recorded here rather than omitted, because a design that only keeps the measurements which flatter it is not a design record.

═══ ⭐⭐ AND IT WAS NEVER GOING TO VALIDATE, FOR THREE REASONS ═══

**1. THE SAMPLE IS SMALL BECAUSE THE GRAPH IS A STAR.** Only 15 of 72 edges have both ends inside the split systems; 57 reach outside. The adopt trial measured why: fan-in `foundation` 49, `graph` 42, `nodes` 41, and 45% of core modules importing ONLY those three hubs. Most dependencies point at the foundation, not at siblings, so intra-system cohesion has little to be computed from.

**2. THE DOMINANT CROSS-EDGE IS THE CUT WORKING.** `Telling -> Finding` at 4 edges is the reports depending on the detectors — a DIRECTED LAYER dependency, and exactly what the observability cut predicts: the instrument is separate from the presenter, and the presenter reads the instrument. **A layered carving MAXIMISES cross-group edges by construction**, and modularity metrics penalise them regardless of direction. Scoring a layered architecture on undirected modularity measures the wrong thing.

**3. IT IS THE THIRD INDEPENDENT ROUTE TO ONE CONCLUSION.** The adopt trial (2026-08-25) found the functional carving unrecoverable from source, by directory and by imports. The co-change experiment (2026-08-21) found **71% of the strongest maintainability signal crossing subsystem boundaries**. This finds 80% of the dependency signal crossing the new groups. Three different signals, three different days, one conclusion: **reflow2's functional decomposition is not its coupling-optimal decomposition, and `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` chose that deliberately in 2026-07-23.**

📌 WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY TEST THE GROUPING, and it has NOT been done: whether a change to one group forces changes in another — co-change restricted to these components, computable today from 500+ ChangeEvents. Dependency coupling tests a property the carving never claimed to optimise. **Do not read this fact as evidence the split was wrong; read it as evidence that this is the wrong instrument for judging it.**

⚠️ BOUNDS: one design, one day, one direction. Edges counted are `DEPENDS_ON` between Components only — not capability coupling (which holds ONE edge across 212 capabilities and can measure nothing), and not co-change. No comparison against an alternative grouping was run, so nothing here says another carving would score better.
